questions.prompt: In Claude's Agent SDK, what does the description of a subagent tell Claude?

options.text: Which model the subagent runs on and how much money it may spend
options.explanation: The model is a separate setting. The description is about when to use the agent.

options.text: When the main agent should pick this subagent for a given task
options.explanation: Right. The docs describe it as a natural language description of when to use this agent.

options.text: Which tools the subagent is allowed to call during a run
options.explanation: Tools are a separate setting called tools.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI say about the short note that tells a model when to hand work to a specialist?

options.text: Keep it short and concrete, so the choice is easy for the model to make
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says to keep the handoff description short and concrete.

options.text: Make it as long as the specialist's own full instructions, so nothing is lost
options.explanation: OpenAI says to keep it short. The long instructions belong to the specialist.

options.text: Leave it empty and let the model guess the right specialist
options.explanation: OpenAI says to write a short, concrete description. It helps the model choose.

questions.prompt: What does Claude say you get from limiting the tools of a subagent?

options.text: A larger context window for the subagent
options.explanation: Tool limits do not change the context window.

options.text: A lower price on every call that the subagent makes
options.explanation: Tool limits are not a pricing setting.

options.text: Less risk of unintended actions by the agent
options.explanation: Right. Claude says subagents can be limited to specific tools, which reduces the risk of unintended actions.
